key_insight: AdsNet predicts adsorption energies directly from local atomic graphs, combining geometric sensitivity with computation that does not scale with total system size.
engineering_relevance: The model could accelerate catalyst screening and local interface relaxation without evaluating full-system machine-learning potentials.
method: Build a cutoff-based graph of adsorbate atoms and their immediate surface neighbors.
Use equivariant message passing with scalar and vector features to predict adsorption energy and per-atom contributions.
Obtain analytic forces through automatic differentiation for projected-gradient relaxation with adaptive line search.
evidence_signal: Trained on 33,920 DFT structures spanning 26 transition metals and six adsorbates, AdsNet reports an energy RMSE of 0.032 eV and a force RMSE of 0.047 eV/Å.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish generalization to unseen surface chemistries or environments where interactions beyond the local cutoff matter.
paper_title: AdsNet: A Graph Neural Network for Direct Adsorption Energy Prediction
